gold: Every authored or modified test file proves meaningful success and a relevant negative outcome for its actual subject, establishing usable setup rather than token coverage. Every changed non-controller expect-based test has exactly one direct expect proving its intended observable contract without hidden assertions or synthetic bundles. Controller tests retain meaningful direct status/body assertions, and native node:assert tests retain their framework. Independently evolving workflows and distinct scenarios remain explicit; all non-empty expected objects, including single-property and partial-matcher objects, stay multiline. Required transition, race, and rollback evidence is preserved. Structural compliance alone never proves semantic quality.

rubric.question: Review every complete changed test in the supplied scope, not only edited lines. If the changed-test scope is missing or incomplete, return BLOCKED with the exact missing evidence.

Apply Scenario-Oriented Verification and Structured Controller Query Inputs in docs/references/code-organization-reference.md to actual changed controller suites. Preserve outer source-path scopes; require the bare class and exactly #action - METHOD - /url-pattern with both separators, checking the actual action/routing declaration and equivalent suites within authorized changed-test scope. Do not impose controller names on unrelated subjects. Prefer nested query data and native .query(object) only with installed client/version and parser evidence of equivalent nested filters, arrays and ordering. Retain existing qs.stringify for demonstrated nested-array limitations and intentional raw/malformed-wire or encoding-contract tests. Require real request assertions distinguishing filtering/sort behavior when migrating, not status alone. Cite exact location, governing source, client/routing evidence and behavior-preserving correction for FAIL; missing necessary context yields BLOCKED. Do not add dependencies, change parsing for style, or audit unrelated tests.

Apply Project-Root Imports and Paths in docs/references/code-organization-reference.md only to authorized changed tests. Assess dependency groups independently of direct subject imports. Use the explicit conventions that govern the file, not the project name, alias spellings, or conventions from another project. Where local guidance separates domain dependencies from a unified factories/request-support group, FAIL either violation: mixing a model with factories or separating factories from request support with a blank line. Cite the misplaced imports, governing guidance, and exact grouping correction. Accept the corrected header, including router-driven tests without a controller import. If the applicable guidance does not specify that grouping, do not enforce it. Separately determine the actual primary subject from Act/assertions. When directly exercising a subject with a supported default export, require that default import in a dedicated group after factories/test support unless explicit local guidance overrides the placement or import form. FAIL a named CreateCsvService import among support dependencies when those conditions apply; cite the exact import and default-import/group correction. PASS the corrected group, supporting named imports, named-only subjects, explicit local overrides, and mixed-subject tests without evidence of one primary subject. Never require an unused subject import or invent an export. Preserve public paths and initialization order. If source, export, or guidance evidence needed for a decision is unavailable, return BLOCKED and name what is missing.

Apply Meaningful Scenarios and Subject Ownership and CLI Scenario Ownership and Shared Mechanics in the supplied assertion-quality source. Judge each complete changed test file against its actual subject and material setup; if that consumer evidence is missing, name it and return BLOCKED. Identify the successful control and relevant negative outcome, not names or counts. Name files and describe scopes for the actual asserted subject. FAIL a boolean/flag matrix that selects DRAFT versus APPROVED state and estimated versus actual itinerary payload keys; accept separately named explicit scenarios with literal state, payload, local fixtures and retained assertions. Do not replace the flag with helper-driven workflow dispatch. Prefer explicit concrete missing-association scenarios with literal expectations; identical Act/assertion shapes alone do not justify computed property/error machinery. Distinguish reusable isolated setup, writers, Git/subprocess runners, parsing and cleanup from a multi-mode builder hiding material provider/check configuration, baseline source, post-baseline changes/deletion or paging/recovery variants. Keep those choices visible in each scenario; named flags alone do not repair hidden ownership. Accept homogeneous literal parser/argument cases and necessary sequential command lifecycles. Preserve actual stdout/stderr/exit, retained-error and transition observations, security-sensitive isolation, native node:assert multiple assertions, and supported test-script discovery if files move. Reject artificial aggregate assertion objects and trivial file-per-assert fragmentation. If handwritten prose serves only as a row title, prefer standalone literal behavioral titles with each setup and assertion visible. Do not split a homogeneous table merely for interpolating an actual input or expected value. Retain readable homogeneous transformation tables, shared infrastructure and genuine shared invariants.

Apply Human Readability in docs/references/code-organization-reference.md: all non-empty expected object literals, including single-property assertion objects and partial-matcher arguments, put each property on its own line even within formatter width. Preserve literal values, order, and matcher semantics. Ordinary small single-field call arguments may remain compact; assertion data is not that exception. Do not demand matcher replacement or unrelated formatting.

Apply exactly one direct expect per non-controller expect-based test as the shared default, not a local opt-in or at-most-one rule: zero and multiple calls violate it. Asymmetric matcher factories are not additional direct expect calls. Preserve native node:assert/assert/strict assertions rather than requiring a framework migration; native assertions elsewhere in a file do not exempt an expect-based test or an assertion-free test. Identify governing ordinary-language local standards and cite their source; report genuine conflicts truthfully. If required guidance is unavailable, return BLOCKED rather than guessing.

Assess whether the single expectation proves the named behavior through a natural real result or meaningful native matcher. Preserve native promise rejection assertions, web-first matchers, meaningful nested matchers, and direct comparisons of actual returned, fetched, or persisted objects and arrays. Accept readable inline asymmetric matcher trees and simple awaited actual-result queries; reject one-use matcher/query staging imposed solely by the construction default, while preserving meaningful reuse, sequencing, scope/options, and evaluation count. Do not move required operations or manufacture assertions. Prefer a complete natural contract such as a route fullPath where appropriate. Reject fabricated summary objects, weakened payloads, and bundled .mock.calls; exact count alone is not semantic proof.

Identify independent outcomes or saves bundled in one test, and assertions hidden in Arrange, Act, helpers, or hooks. Independent saves need separate focused tests using API spies and concrete expected payloads, not expect.anything() payloads or bundled call arrays. Preserve transition/race/rollback setup, causal sequences, and scenario identities in each focused test that needs them; do not remove earlier operations or weaken observations to satisfy count. Inspect invoked helpers and relevant scenario context when needed; if required context is unavailable, return BLOCKED. Irrelevant absent callers or optional siblings are not required context.

Apply the controller exception only to paths with a controller/ or controllers/ directory segment (case-insensitive), or filenames ending .controller.test/spec.<JS/TS extension>, -controller.test/spec.<extension>, _controller.test/spec.<extension>, or Controller.test/spec.<extension> with the PascalCase suffix. Never infer controller status from HTTP usage or a response variable. Preserve clear direct status/body controller assertions or a meaningful response matcher; keep independent persistence effects separate. A coupled invariant is not a general multi-expect exception for non-controller tests, and allow-multiple-expects is not a bypass. Preserve supported explicit scoped suppressions. Each finding must cite the test and governing guidance, identify the count violation or semantic gap, and offer a concrete correction without inventing findings.
